text:
emma (PM): Heads up — customer X asked for a clear migration path for function-calling + structured outputs in both Python and TS SDKs. They want examples, types, and a changelog entry before we mark the API stable.

mike (SDK Eng): Noted. I can add TS types and a Python wrapper, but need to scope examples. Do we want: 1) simple function call example, 2) nested structured output, 3) error/edge-case example?

anna (DevEx): +1 on those three. Also add a short tutorial showing how to map a model response to a typed dataclass / interface. Most customers copy-paste examples, so make them copy-ready. :memo:

kevin (Docs): For changelog, propose a single entry: "function-calling: stable v1 — typing and examples" with links to the example notebook + migration notes. We should include a small migration checklist: deprecated fields, new signatures, recommended fallbacks.

emma (PM): Launch criteria (what Product needs):
- Examples for both SDKs in the repo + runnable notebook
- TS types exported and documented, Python typing hints + mypy-friendly usage
- Changelog entry + short migration guide
- Internal e2e test + one external beta customer signoff

raj (ML Eng): FYI backend changed the function-calling contract a bit: the tool metadata now includes `response_schema` and optional `confidence`. SDKs must preserve that shape. If SDK maps it differently, we need a compatibility layer.

mike (SDK Eng): Can we punt the `confidence` field into `metadata` on the Python side? Types would be `Dict[str, Any]` unless we create a typed wrapper. For TS I can define:
```ts
export type ToolResponse = {
  name: string;
  payload: unknown;
  response_schema?: Record<string, any>;
  confidence?: number;
};
```
Keep it minimal but typed.

kevin (Docs): That TS type is perfect to show in the docs. For Python, suggest dataclass example:
```py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Optional, Dict

@dataclass
class ToolResponse:
    name: str
    payload: Any
    response_schema: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    confidence: Optional[float] = None
```
Then show mapping from raw model JSON to this class.

tom (Backend): We'll keep the old shape for 30 days and serve both `tool_response` and `tool_response_v2` fields to ease migration. We can set a deprecation header that SDKs surface.

anna (DevEx): Good — we should add a short snippet showing detection of both shapes, something like: `if 'tool_response_v2' in resp: ... else: ...` in examples. That reduces breakage for customers who don't upgrade immediately.

emma (PM): Prioritization question: two tracks — (A) docs + examples + changelog (high priority), (B) full typed SDK surface + tests (medium). Customers want immediate examples; some asked for typed SDKs before GA. Thoughts on time estimates?

mike (SDK Eng): Estimate: TS typings + example change and release in 4 dev-days. Python typing + dataclass glue + tests 6 dev-days. Changelog + docs updates 2 dev-days (kevin/anna). End-to-end test and canary with beta customer ~3 dev-days (tom/qa).

kevin (Docs): I can draft the migration guide and changelog in 2 business days, but need the code samples merged to reference.

emma (PM): Proposed plan: ship docs/examples + changelog in first release (week 1), then SDK typed surface + tests in week 2, followed by canary + beta signoff. If that's acceptable, I'll mark as priority and schedule resources.

sara (Product): Customer success flagged this as high impact for two enterprise deals. Recommend accelerating SDK typing to week 1 if we can reallocate a dev. Otherwise the docs-first plan is OK but communicate timeline to customers.

mike (SDK Eng): I can try to compress TS work into 1.5 days if Kevin and Anna can review examples quickly. Python still needs 4–5 days.

raj (ML Eng): Minor heads-up: our inference runtime may change the `response_schema` representation in the next infra deploy (1769212000). If that lands, we may need to tweak the examples. Can we freeze the example payload shape today?

tom (Backend): I can gate the infra change behind a feature flag for 1 week so docs stay stable. Will coordinate with infra team.

ci-bot: New branch `sdk/fn-calls-examples` created by mike. CI will run tests.

anna (DevEx): Ok, action items:
- mike: land TS types + examples in `sdk/fn-calls-examples` (ETA 1.5d)
- mike: create Python PR with dataclass + mapping (ETA 4d)
- kevin: draft changelog & migration guide (ETA 2d)
- tom: gate infra change behind FF and run canary (ETA 3d)
- emma: notify enterprise customers of timeline and get one beta signoff (ETA 1d)

kevin (Docs): I'll include a short section in the migration guide titled "Quick fix for older SDKs" with a one-liner: `resp = resp.get('tool_response_v2') or resp.get('tool_response')`.

emma (PM): Thanks. Please update the PR descriptions with the launch checklist items so QA can verify. I'll follow up in the morning to lock owners. :calendar: 

mike (SDK Eng): Will do. Adding `needs-docs` label to my PR now.

sara (Product): :thumbsup: keep me posted, I'm gating two deals on this.

anna (DevEx): Small UX ask — add runnable snippets in both repo examples and a quick REPL-friendly one-liner for the TS client (one import, one call). People love single-line copy-paste.

kevin (Docs): Agreed. I'll create a minimal gist-style example for the top of the guide.

emma (PM): Closing loop — we'll treat docs/examples as the release anchor and SDK typing as follow-up in the next patch if needed. If any blocker appears, ping here. Thanks everyone.
